Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

charm noun

attractiveness

also charming manner, grace, loveliness

classical

Prop. 1.2.29: ūnica nec dēsit jūcundīs grātia verbīs (Lewis & Short)
Ov. M. 7.44: grātia fōrmae (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 150

grātia, grātiae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

grace, charm

In this sense, charm or loveliness, Lewis & Short finds it only in poetry and in prose after Augustus, most often in Quintilian; in Cicero grātia is favour, influence or thanks. For charm of manner in classical prose, lepōs.

Other words

  • lepōs (lepor), lepōris m. — charm, grace, attractiveness

    noun, third declension · classical · Plaut. Poen. 1.2.32: sine omnī lepōre et sine suāvitāte (Lewis & Short s.v. lepor); Cic. Verr. 2.5.142: affluēns omnī lepōre ac venustāte (Lewis & Short); Traupman 289 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • amoenitās, amoenitātis f. — pleasantness, loveliness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 150; Lewis & Short: “pleasantness, delightfulness, loveliness”, of places; Traupman 289 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: mostly of places.

  • decor, decōris m. — grace, comeliness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 150 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: a poetic word, in prose perhaps not before the Augustan period, and frequent in Quintilian.

See also attractive, amulet.
